W1 (mechanism), after E002.

Measured so far
- E001, 9 epochs: accuracy 0.7430, time 9.43 s.
- E002, 10 epochs: accuracy 0.7495, time 10.55 s.

So one extra epoch costs about 1.1 s. The fixed cost is small, about 0.3 s or less: uint8 to GPU, cast, pad, eigh on 5k images. A naive linear fit even makes it slightly negative, which is noise. The run is therefore almost purely epochs × 48 steps × per-step cost. H3 and H3.2 are weak levers. Training already drops the ragged batch (50000 // 1024 = 48 steps per epoch), so I006 has nothing to fix.

How accuracy arises
- The slope is about +0.65 pp per epoch near 9-10 epochs, which matches my prior of about 0.6. We are still on the steep part of the sample-starved curve. The curve should flatten a little, to about 0.5 pp per epoch near 11.
- On the eager recipe, 0.753 needs about 10.6-11 epochs, roughly 11.2-11.7 s. A 0.755 margin needs about 11.3 epochs.
- Cutting information per sample costs accuracy roughly in proportion. Examples:
  - lower resolution, which also causes a train/test mismatch at 32 px eval;
  - larger batch, which means fewer updates. Muon at batch 2000 gives about 25 steps per epoch.
- Free regularisers such as Lookahead/EMA and the final-weight average are worth about +0.1-0.4 pp, which is roughly 0.3-0.5 epoch.

How time arises (GPU-bound per step)
- Conv FLOPs dominate. Memory-bound BN, GELU and residual-add work in fp16 is perhaps 25-35% of the step.
- torch.compile fusion of BN+GELU+add should cut per-step time by about 12-22%. max-autotune adds little over cuDNN, which is already tuned.
- Fused or foreach SGD saves about 1-2%. CUDA graphs save under 3%, because a 1024-batch step is long compared with launch latency, even with 4 CPUs.

Plan
1. Compile, giving about 0.9 s per epoch.
2. Add epochs to about 11, giving about 10.0-10.3 s at 0.753-0.755.
3. Then trade EMA gains for fewer epochs.

Noise (still prior, not measured)
- Per-seed accuracy std is about 0.2-0.35 pp, so the 3-seed mean has std of about 0.15-0.2 pp. The 0.65 pp step from E001 to E002 is well resolved. Effects of 0.2 pp are not resolvable from a single 3-seed run.
- Time drift is about 1-2%.
- For safety over 40 seeds, target a 3-seed mean of 0.755 or more.

Unsure
(a) How much compile actually gives on this net. The 5-15% vs 20%+ outcomes change the plan.
(b) Whether the port carries a hidden accuracy loss compared with reference airbench96. Candidates are the whitening eps, the lr scaling and the BN eps of 1e-12 in fp16. Fixing one could free 0.5-1 pp.
(c) Whether Lookahead's gain is real at 10 epochs, or within noise.

forecasts.reason: Fusing the memory-bound BN, GELU and residual work cuts the step by about 15%, and the math is unchanged, so accuracy stays near 0.7495.
I expect EMA to add about 0.1-0.3 pp. With a 0.15-0.2 pp std on the 3-seed mean, one run cannot resolve a 0.2 pp threshold. The range also covers the ambiguity of running at 9 vs 10 epochs.
The run is a GPU-bound, deterministic-shape workload, so time should repeat within 2%. Per-seed std should fall around 0.2-0.3 pp.
Training already uses 48 full batches per epoch with no ragged batch, so there is no 0.3 s to save over the compiled port.
Halving the update count at a sample-starved 10 epochs, plus an untuned port, likely loses accuracy. The Newton-Schulz overhead eats much of the gain from the larger batch.

There is less information per sample, plus a resolution mismatch. Small-resolution convs underuse the A100, so the time saving is about 12-15% while accuracy drops 0.5-1 pp, well beyond the 0.2 pp allowed.

cruxes: How much does torch.compile cut per-epoch time on this port: about 10% or more than 20%? This sets whether about 11 epochs fits under about 10 s.
Is there a port-vs-reference accuracy gap (whitening eps, lr scaling at batch 1024, BN eps in fp16) worth 0.5 pp or more that would remove about 1 epoch?
What is the measured per-seed accuracy std? It sets whether a 3-seed mean of 0.753 or 0.756 is needed, which is about 0.5 epoch, or 0.5 s.
